#!/bin/bash
#FLUX --queue=epyc_ssd       # the requested queue
#FLUX --nodes=1              # number of nodes to use
#FLUX --tasks-per-node=1
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=4      #
#FLUX --mem=8000M	     # in megabytes, unless unit explicitly stated
#FLUX --error=logs/{id}.err         # redirect stderr to this file
#FLUX --output=logs/{id}.out        # redirect stdout to this file
# NOTE: The --mail-user and --mail-type directives have been omitted as Flux
# does not have a direct equivalent for job status email notifications.
 
 
echo "Some Usable Environment Variables:"
echo "================================="
echo "hostname=$(hostname)"
# The SLURM variables have been replaced with their Flux equivalents.
echo \$FLUX_JOB_ID=${FLUX_JOB_ID}
echo \$FLUX_JOB_NUM_TASKS=${FLUX_JOB_NUM_TASKS}
echo \$FLUX_JOB_NTASKS_PER_NODE=${FLUX_JOB_NTASKS_PER_NODE}
echo \$FLUX_JOB_CPUS_PER_TASK=${FLUX_JOB_CPUS_PER_TASK}
echo \$FLUX_JOB_NCPUS=${FLUX_JOB_NCPUS}
echo \$SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE=${FLUX_JOB_MEM_PER_NODE} # Note: SLURM is in MB, Flux is in KiB

module purge
module load nextflow/21.10
module load singularity/3.8.7

export NXF_OPTS="-Xms500M -Xmx2G"

workdir="/tmp"
installdir="/mnt/data/GROUP-smbpk/sbidp3/AMRplusplus"
resultsdir="/mnt/data/GROUP-smbpk/sbidp3/AMRplus-all-out"
run="DANS-AMR_April_bracken"

#mkdir ${workdir}/${run}/ 
#mkdir ${workdir}/${run}/fastq/ 
#rsync -rv sbidp3@archive.bios.cf.ac.uk:/mnt/archive/GROUP-smbpk/PROJECTS-DATASTORE/AMR/AMR_monitoring/raw_data/${run}/*gz ${workdir}/${run}/fastq/

cd ${installdir}
# The SLURM_JOB_ID variable is replaced with the Flux equivalent.
nextflow run ${installdir}/main_AMR++.nf \
	-w "${workdir}/${run}/work" \
	-c "${installdir}/config/test_singularity_slurm.config" \
	--reads "${workdir}/${run}/fastq/*{R1,R2}.fastq.gz" \
	--pipeline kraken_and_bracken \
	--output "${workdir}/${run}/bracken" \
	-with-report "${workdir}/${run}/${run}.html" \
	-with-trace "${installdir}/logs/${FLUX_JOB_ID}.trace.txt" \
	-resume

#module load multiqc/1.9
#multiqc -o ${workdir}/${run}/${run}-outputs/Results/ ${workdir}/${run}/${run}-outputs

####
# Results copyout
####
#mkdir ${resultsdir}/${run}
#rsync -r ${workdir}/${run}/${run}-outputs//HostRemoval/NonHostFastq $resultsdir/$run/
#rsync -r ${workdir}/${run}/${run}-outputs/Results $resultsdir/$run/
#rsync ${workdir}/${run}/${run}.html $resultsdir/$run/

## Delete all
#rm -rf ${workdir}/${run}

issues: The informational `echo` command `echo \$SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE=${FLUX_JOB_MEM_PER_NODE}` contains a typo; it should reference `FLUX_JOB_MEM_PER_NODE`, not `SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE`.
The output and error files are directed to a subdirectory (`logs/`). The script does not create this directory, which will cause the job to fail at launch if the directory does not exist.

The `nextflow` command references a configuration file (`test_singularity_slurm.config`). This config file is likely written for a Slurm environment and may contain Slurm-specific directives for submitting sub-jobs. To run correctly under Flux, this configuration file will need to be adapted or replaced with one that uses `flux submit` commands for its sub-jobs.
